meta.mechanism: CETP inhibitor (potent); off-target adrenal aldosterone/cortisol release and blood-pressure elevation
meta.indication: secondary prevention / high cardiovascular risk (CVD or type 2 diabetes) on atorvastatin

n_randomized.quote: We conducted a randomized, double-blind study involving 15,067 patients at high cardiovascular risk.
n_randomized.note: 7533 torcetrapib+atorvastatin, 7534 atorvastatin only. Registry S2: 15067 ACTUAL.

median_followup.quote: At the end of the study on December 2, 2006, the median follow-up in each group was 550 days.

primary_endpoint.value: Time to first major cardiovascular event: death from coronary heart disease, nonfatal MI, stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary outcome was the time to the first major cardiovascular event, which was defined as death from coronary heart disease, nonfatal myocardial infarction, stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina.
primary_endpoint.note: Unstable angina hospitalization was added by protocol amendment 'to increase the number of events and thus increase the statistical power'.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age 45-75 y with CVD (MI, stroke, ACS, UA, PVD, revascularization) 30 days-5 years before screening, or type 2 diabetes; atorvastatin run-in to LDL-C target; uncontrolled hypertension (>140/90) excluded
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Men and women between the ages of 45 and 75 years were eligible to participate in the study if they had a history of cardiovascular disease (including myocardial infarction, stroke, acute coronary syndrome, unstable angina, peripheral vascular disease, and cardiac revascularization) 30 days to 5 years before screening. Patients with type 2 diabetes without previous cardiovascular disease who met American Diabetes Association criteria or were receiving hypoglycemic agents were also eligible.

planned_events.quote: On the basis of the modified primary outcome in the amended protocol and on the increased number of patients, the number of primary outcomes at an average follow-up of 4.5 years was expected to be 1820.
planned_events.note: Original design: 13,000 patients, 551 vs 433 primary outcomes (984 total).

assumed_rrr.quote: The original design assumed a sample size of 13,000 patients (6500 per treatment group) to yield 551 primary outcomes in the atorvastatin-only group (8.48%) and 433 in the group receiving both atorvastatin and torcetrapib (6.66%) after an average of 4.5 years of follow-up — in other words, an absolute reduction of 1.82 percentage points or a relative reduction of 21% in the cumulative incidence.
assumed_rrr.note: Assumption of the original (pre-amendment) design; no revised RRR stated for the amended protocol.

power.quote: This number of patients would provide a statistical power of 90% to detect a treatment difference in the primary efficacy analysis at the two-sided level of 0.05 with the use of a log-rank test.

alpha.quote: at the two-sided level of 0.05 with the use of a log-rank test
alpha.note: Safety-monitoring boundary: P<0.01 (unadjusted) on all-cause death.

stopped_early.quote: This trial was terminated prematurely on December 2, 2006, in a decision made by the sponsor on the basis of the recommendation of the trial's independent steering committee, which was acting on advice from the independent data and safety monitoring board.
stopped_early.note: Stopped for harm (excess deaths and CV events). 837 primary events (464 + 373) vs 1820 expected (~46%); efficacy boundary (after ~50% of events) never reached. Pfizer release S3: 'recommended terminating the study because of an imbalance of mortality and cardiovascular events'.

baseline.note: Read from Table 1 image: atorvastatin-only 79.9±20.4, torcetrapib 79.7±20.4 mg/dL (after atorvastatin run-in).

biomarker_effects.quote: At 12 months in patients who received torcetrapib, there was an increase of 72.1% in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and a decrease of 24.9% in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, as compared with baseline
biomarker_effects.note: 72.1% is from baseline. Placebo-adjusted 70.3 points computed by curator from Table 2 image (+72.1±34.7 vs +1.8±14.0). At 3 months +60.9 vs +1.7.

biomarker_effects.method: not verified (Tall & Rader table: 'LDL measured indirectly')
biomarker_effects.quote: a decrease of 24.9% in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, as compared with baseline
biomarker_effects.note: Placebo-adjusted -27.9 points computed by curator from Table 2 image (-24.9±28.5 vs +3.0±23.7). Absolute 12-mo: -21.5 vs +0.9 mg/dL. CETP-inhibitor LDL-C by routine methods is biased (cf. Davidson 2013).
Computed by curator from Table 2 image: apoB % change -12.5±19.2 (torcetrapib) vs +2.0±16.6 (atorvastatin only); absolute -10.1±14.4 vs +0.6±11.1 mg/dL. Not measured at 12 months (NA).

biomarker_effects.quote: Treatment with 120 mg of torcetrapib daily increased plasma concentrations of HDL cholesterol by 61 percent (P<0.001) and 46 percent (P=0.001) in the atorvastatin and non-atorvastatin cohorts, respectively
biomarker_effects.note: Change vs the preceding placebo period, not a parallel placebo arm.

biomarker_effects.quote: Torcetrapib also reduced low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels by 17 percent in the atorvastatin cohort (P=0.02).

The percent change from baseline to Week 8 with torcetrapib (least-squares mean difference from placebo) was dose-dependent and ranged from 9.0% to 54.5% for HDL-C (p < or = 0.0001 for 30 mg and higher doses) and from 3.0% to -16.5% for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) (p < 0.01 for 90-mg dose).
biomarker_effects.note: ILLUMINATE dose (60 mg) value not in abstract.

biomarker_effects.quote: from 3.0% to -16.5% for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) (p < 0.01 for 90-mg dose)
biomarker_effects.note: At 60 mg, LDL-C change was 0.1% (TG>150) vs -22.2% (TG<=150) per abstract.

biomarker_effects.timepoint: 8 weeks (90 mg on atorvastatin 20 mg; 8.3% at 10 mg)
biomarker_effects.quote: After 8 weeks, the percent change from baseline with torcetrapib (least-squares mean difference from placebo) ranged from 8.3% to 40.2% for HDL-C (p < or = 0.0001 for 30-mg and higher doses) and from 0.6% to -18.9% for LDL-C (p < 0.01 for 60-mg and 90-mg doses).
from 0.6% to -18.9% for LDL-C (p < 0.01 for 60-mg and 90-mg doses)

hr.quote: There was also an increased risk of cardiovascular events (hazard ratio, 1.25; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09 to 1.44; P=0.001)

events_treatment.quote: Panel B shows the between-group comparison of patients who had the primary composite outcome: 373 patients in the atorvastatin-only group and 464 patients in the torcetrapib group.

events_control.quote: 373 patients in the atorvastatin-only group and 464 patients in the torcetrapib group

safety_signals.quote: At study termination, there were 93 deaths in the torcetrapib group and 59 in the atorvastatin-only group, for a hazard ratio of 1.58 in the torcetrapib group (95% CI, 1.14 to 2.19; P=0.006).
safety_signals.note: Contemporaneous reports of the DSMB data cited 82 vs 51 deaths (not verified in a primary source).

safety_signals.value: Systolic BP +5.4 mmHg at 12 months (+4.5 vs atorvastatin only)
safety_signals.quote: an increase of 5.4 mm Hg in systolic blood pressure
safety_signals.note: Table 2 image: SBP 12-mo +5.4±13.2 vs +0.9±11.5; DBP +2.0 vs -0.1. Footnote: SBP rise >15 mmHg in 19.5% vs 9.4% at 12 months.

safety_signals.value: Aldosterone increased (upper percentiles 9.5/11.0/14.0 vs 8.6/10.0/13.0 ng/dL at 3 months)
safety_signals.quote: At 3 months, these percentiles were 8.6, 10.0, and 13.0 ng per deciliter in the atorvastatin-only group and 9.5, 11.0, and 14.0 ng per deciliter in the torcetrapib group (P<0.001).
safety_signals.note: Measured post hoc after termination; >50% of samples below quantification limit, so means not comparable.

safety_signals.value: Electrolytes: potassium down, sodium and bicarbonate up (mineralocorticoid pattern)
safety_signals.quote: In the torcetrapib group, as compared with the atorvastatin-only group, there were greater increases in levels of sodium (1.39 mmol per liter and 0.78 mmol per liter, respectively) and bicarbonate (2.28 mmol per liter and 1.93 mmol per liter, respectively; P<0.001).
safety_signals.note: Potassium at 12 months -0.08 vs +0.06 mmol/L. Post hoc: higher death risk when potassium fall or bicarbonate rise exceeded the median.

safety_signals.value: Off-target pressor effect and aldosterone release independent of CETP (animal / adrenal-cell data)
safety_signals.quote: Torcetrapib evoked an acute increase in blood pressure in all species evaluated whereas no increase was observed with anacetrapib.
safety_signals.note: Also: 'Treatment with torcetrapib was associated with an increase in plasma levels of aldosterone and corticosterone and, in vitro, was shown to release aldosterone from adrenocortical cells.'

safety_signals.quote: Significant blood pressure increases were noted in 2 of 140 subjects.
safety_signals.note: McKenney 2006 (S6): 'In some treatment groups, small increases in systolic and diastolic blood pressures were noted.' ILLUMINATE authors: the 5.4 mmHg rise was 'a greater effect than had been observed in earlier studies of shorter duration'.

genetics.finding: Homozygous CETP deficiency (Japanese splice mutation) causes very high HDL-C and low LDL-C/apoB; no premature atherosclerosis observed in affected families.
genetics.quote: There was no evidence of premature atherosclerosis in the families with CETP deficiency.

genetics.finding: CETP mutations (D442G, intron 14G:A) in Honolulu Heart Program men raised HDL-C but were associated with MORE CHD (contradictory genetic signal pre-ILLUMINATE).
genetics.quote: The relative risk (RR) of CHD was 1.43 in men with mutations (P < .05); after adjustment for CHD risk factors, the RR was 1.55 (P = .02)

genetics.finding: CETP TaqIB variant: higher HDL-C and lower CAD risk; association lost after HDL-C adjustment.
genetics.quote: TaqIB genotype was significantly associated with the risk of CAD (odds ratio=0.78 [0.66 to 0.93]) in B2B2 individuals compared with B1B1 individuals (P for linearity=0.008). Additional adjustment for HDL-C levels rendered a loss of statistical significance (P=0.4).

genetics.finding: Common CETP variants (TaqIB, I405V, -629C>A) that modestly lower CETP activity and raise HDL-C are weakly associated with lower coronary risk (meta-analysis, 27,196 cases).
genetics.effect: per-allele OR for coronary disease 0.95 (0.92-0.99) for TaqIB
genetics.quote: The combined per-allele odds ratios (ORs) for coronary disease were 0.95 (95% CI, 0.92-0.99) for TaqIB, 0.94 (95% CI, 0.89-1.00) for I405V, and 0.95 (95% CI, 0.91-1.00) for -629C>A.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: genetically raised HDL-C (LIPG Asn396Ser; 14-SNP HDL score) does not lower MI risk; LDL score does.
genetics.effect: LIPG 396Ser OR 0.99 (0.88-1.11); HDL genetic score OR per 1 SD 0.93 (0.68-1.26)
genetics.quote: However, a 1 SD increase in HDL cholesterol due to genetic score was not associated with risk of myocardial infarction (OR 0·93, 95% CI 0·68-1·26, p=0·63).

genetics.finding: Rare CETP protein-truncating variants (1 in 975 carriers) raise HDL-C, lower LDL-C and triglycerides, and are associated with lower CHD risk.
genetics.quote: CETP PTV carrier status was associated with reduced risk for CHD (summary odds ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval, 0.54-0.90; P=5.1×10-3).

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: CETP genetic score lowers CV risk in proportion to apoB reduction; on a statin (HMGCR) background the apoB reduction and the risk reduction are attenuated, so benefit tracks apoB, not LDL-C or HDL-C.
genetics.effect: CETP score alone OR 0.946 (0.921-0.972); combined with HMGCR score OR 0.985 (0.955-1.015)
genetics.quote: When combined with the HMGCR score, the CETP score was associated with the same reduction in LDL-C levels but an attenuated reduction in apoB levels and a corresponding attenuated nonsignificant risk of major cardiovascular events (OR, 0.985 [95% CI, 0.955-1.015]).

consensus_explanation.summary: Torcetrapib's harm is attributed to molecule-specific off-target toxicity, not CETP inhibition: it raised blood pressure (~5 mmHg), stimulated adrenal aldosterone (and cortisol) release with a mineralocorticoid electrolyte pattern (low K, high Na/HCO3), and mortality was concentrated in patients with the largest electrolyte shifts. Animal and adrenal-cell studies showed the pressor/aldosterone effect is independent of CETP (occurs in species lacking CETP; absent with anacetrapib). Later CETP inhibitors without this effect (dalcetrapib, evacetrapib, anacetrapib) showed no harm, and anacetrapib (REVEAL) gave modest benefit. In addition, the HDL-C rise was not causally protective and the apoB reduction (~14%) was modest, so even without toxicity only a small benefit was expected.
